claim: Random teams of agents beat teams of the individually best agents in the Hong-Page ring simulation (94.53 vs 92.56 for 10 agents l=12; 94.72 vs 93.78 for 20 agents; 96.08 vs 93.52 at l=20), but only under stated conditions (hard problem, locally optimal agents, large pool); the gap shrinks as teams grow.
agent_test: Compare k samples from different prompts/methods against k samples of the single best prompt at equal tokens on hard search tasks.

claim: The Hong-Page diversity-beats-ability result is fragile: it depends on landscape randomness and on how ability is defined, so it is not a general law (Grim et al. abstract confirmed: sensitivity to landscape randomness).
agent_test: Re-run diversity vs best-single-method teams on tasks of differing ruggedness (code tasks of differing difficulty).

claim: Maverick/follower division-of-labor gains in Weisberg-Muldoon landscape models change with small rule changes; a replication in another language reproduced the code results, but not across parameter space.
agent_test: Background only; do not build agent rules on mavericks without model-specific tests.

claim: In bandit-network models, less-connected scientific communities reach the correct consensus more often (transient diversity), at the cost of speed; the effect weakens on easy problems and is costly on hard ones (Rosenstock et al.).
agent_test: Run parallel branches with delayed vs immediate sharing at equal total tokens; measure final accuracy and tokens to correct.

claim: Exploration is under-supplied because it is a free-rider problem; mild confirmation bias or stubbornness can preserve useful diversity, strong levels cause polarisation.
agent_test: Add a rule that a minority hypothesis is kept for N steps; compare with immediate pruning.

claim: Demographic diversity helps in a simulated community only when out-group trust is moderate and conformity pressure is low; full distrust, full trust and high conformity remove or reverse the gain.
agent_test: In multi-agent debate, vary how much an agent weights peers' answers; check for an interior optimum.

claim: Under Condorcet-style voting, diversity can beat ability, but only above derived thresholds.
agent_test: Informs how to weight votes by independence; not directly testable.

claim: Miscommunication in Hong-Page type teams reduces but usually does not erase the diversity advantage; effects depend on setting.
agent_test: Inject noise into summaries passed between agents and measure the drop.

claim: In humans, underrepresented groups introduce more novel concept links yet receive less uptake and career reward (1.2M US PhDs 1977-2015).
agent_test: Not applicable to one agent; relevant only as a warning about the agent's own novelty discounting in reranking.

claim: Mixed-gender teams produce more novel and more highly cited medical papers than same-gender teams (6.6M papers; large teams 48% vs 44% novel, 10.2% vs 8.9% top-5% cited); ethnic diversity of authors also tracks citations (observational).
agent_test: Observational, human; background only.

claim: Multi-agent LLM systems using different model families as proposers or debaters beat ones using copies of one model in several reports (MoA ablation 61.3 vs 56.7 at n=6; Hegazy 91% vs 82% GSM8K; Heter-MAD +5.8% to +8.2% over averages), though one is a single-author report and one is contradicted by K12.
agent_test: Same-token comparison of heterogeneous vs single-model ensembles on a held-out set.
audit_note: MoA 61.3 vs 56.7 is AlpacaEval LC win rate (multi vs single-proposer copies); Hegazy 91 vs 82 matches; Heter-MAD 5.8% is vs CoT-average and 8.2% vs EoT-average (6.4% vs SoM-average), so the range mixes baselines, a minor slip.

claim: Diversity trades off against quality: when one model is clearly best, sampling it repeatedly (Self-MoA) beats mixing (65.7 vs 59.1 on AlpacaEval 2.0 LC under Li et al.'s setup); mixing helps when models are close in quality.
agent_test: Self-ensemble of the best model vs mixed ensemble at equal tokens; regress on quality and diversity.

claim: Multi-agent debate does not reliably beat chain of thought or self-consistency at equal compute (Multi-Persona won 0% vs CoT; ChatEval and AgentVerse about 15%; single best case +0.85%) and is very sensitive to settings.
schema_part: O (do not use debate as default)
agent_test: Debate vs self-consistency at equal tokens across 5+ benchmarks.
audit_note: Win-rate figures (MP no significant gain, ChatEval/AgentVerse about 15% of 36 configs, +0.85% AgentVerse on MMLU/Claude-3.5-haiku) come from Zhang et al. 2025, not Smit; the +0.85% is an example case, and Smit shows tuned agreement made Multi-Persona the best, which supports the sensitivity point.

claim: Debate beat single-agent, reflection and majority vote in the original report (arithmetic 81.8 vs 67.0; GSM8K 85 vs 77), but later work finds the gain mostly vanishes against strong baselines.
agent_test: See K13; always include self-consistency baseline.

claim: Self-reflection gets stuck on its first answer (degeneration of thought); opposing agents with a judge break this; agents drift to consensus unless made stubborn.
agent_test: Adversarial second pass vs same-agent reflection at equal tokens.

claim: Larger ensembles by plain sampling and voting raise accuracy, with gains largest on hard tasks (GSM8K 12 to 24%, MATH 6 to 10%).
agent_test: Scale sample count at equal tokens against alternatives.

claim: Asking one model for several distinct solution approaches, then ensembling, beat CoT and self-consistency on hard tasks and cut cost (about 4x lower than SC-10, few-shot).
agent_test: Approach-diverse prompting vs plain self-consistency at equal tokens.

claim: LLM outputs are homogeneous: same-model pairs exceed 0.8 embedding similarity in 79% of cases, cross-model 71-82%, decoding tweaks do not fix it (Infinity-Chat, 26K queries, 70+ models); idea generation saturates (about 200 non-duplicates of 4000); epistemic diversity stays below a search baseline.
agent_test: Measure pairwise similarity among branches; if very high, extra branches add little.
audit_note: Slips: the 79% is the share of query response pools (INFINITY-CHAT100, 100 queries x 50 responses) whose mean pairwise similarity exceeds 0.8, not pair counts over all 26K queries; min-p still leaves 61.2% above 0.8; Si et al. 200 of 4000 and the below-search-baseline epistemic-diversity finding match.

claim: Identity-prompted LLMs do not reproduce in-group standpoint views and flatten group variation; temperature does not fix it (3200 participants, 16 identities, 4 LLMs).
agent_test: Test persona branches vs plain branches at equal tokens; do not treat personas as standpoints.

claim: Persona prompts give small gains in debate (MMLU 71.1 to 74.2).
agent_test: Persona branches vs plain at equal tokens.

claim: Multi-agent LLM systems fail often (41% to 86.7% across 7 frameworks, 1642 traces), mostly from design and weak verification.
agent_test: Add a verifier step; count failure modes.

claim: An adversarial generate-debate-rank structure scales with test-time compute in a discovery agent (co-scientist), but review-agent gains are modest and Elo is self-judged.
agent_test: Elo-style pairwise ranking vs single scoring at equal tokens.

claim: LLM-generated research ideas were rated more novel than expert ideas (4.84 vs 5.64) but slightly less feasible, and lack diversity.
agent_test: Track novelty vs feasibility of agent hypotheses.

claim: Shared reliance on AI output risks knowledge collapse and epistemic monocultures in simulation; personalisation mitigates better than randomisation.
agent_test: Track convergence across restarts of one agent.

claim: Longino's four norms (public venues, uptake, shared standards, tempered equality) are philosophical claims without direct empirical tests; they map to critique-and-uptake steps.
agent_test: Implement mandatory uptake of critique; ablate it.

claim: Diversity prediction theorem: collective squared error equals mean individual error minus prediction diversity (identity; squared-error averaging only).
agent_test: Use for ensembles of numeric estimates.

claim: Task-related team diversity helps team performance and bio-demographic diversity does not (Horwitz 2007), and groups under-discuss unshared information (hidden profile); both recalled, unopened.
agent_test: Background only; unverified.

claim: At equal thinking-token budgets above about 500 tokens, a single agent matches or beats five multi-agent designs on multi-hop QA (average accuracy at 2000 tokens: single 0.421, debate 0.403, ensemble 0.372); multi-agent is ahead only at 100 tokens (debate 0.370 vs single 0.290) or when context is damaged. All copies are the same model, so heterogeneity at equal tokens is untested.
agent_test: Run k same-config samples vs k heterogeneous configs at equal total tokens on a discovery-style task; report variance.

claim: Answer-level diversity (distinct candidate answers), not sampling temperature, is what makes debate or voting gain: choosing a diverse initial pool raised Pass@5 from 0.79 to 0.91 (Qwen-7B) and 0.74 to 0.90 (Llama-8B). Embedding diversity per added agent falls (Vendi/N 1.03 to 0.47 from 3 to 7 agents).
agent_test: Select branches for distinct final answers before merging; log Vendi/N per branch count.

claim: Delaying or partitioning sharing (blind writing first, subgroups) keeps semantic diversity higher in LLM groups; no study found here shows this raises final accuracy, so the transient-diversity effect is not shown for LLM agents.
agent_test: Compare immediate vs delayed merge of parallel branches on final accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: A forced exchange step (share facts plus one reason the leader may be wrong, then decide) lifted hidden-profile accuracy from 0.04-0.17 to 0.73-0.80 across three models, but against no protocol, not against free self-critique; plain debate that only adds uptake can instead lower accuracy via conformity.
agent_test: Test a mandatory counter-reason step vs free self-critique at equal tokens.

claim: In MAST, task verification is 21.3% of multi-agent failures and inter-agent misalignment 36.9%; ignoring other agents' input is only 1.9%. Verification fixes give +9.4 to +15.6 points on ChatDev ProgramDev but are not universal, so a verifier agent does not remove failures.
agent_test: Map the 14 modes to guardrails G1-G12; use external checks in the verifier.
